title: Servicing Academy Q&A: Cure Speed and Goodwill on Late Fees
content:
**What is the cure-speed factor?** For goodwill relief on a late fee on Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts, the late fee, once multiplied by its goodwill share, is multiplied by a cure-speed factor. The factor follows the calendar days from the assessment date of the most recent late fee on the contract to the posting date of the most recent scheduled-installment payment on the contract.

| Calendar days from the late fee to the most recent scheduled-installment payment | Treatment of the shared late fee |
|---|---|
| more than 30 | multiplied by the slow-cure goodwill factor, 0.5 |
| 15 to 30 | multiplied by the steady-cure goodwill factor, 0.8 |
| fewer than 15 | kept as it is |

**Which dates are read?** Both come from the loan history: the date of the latest late-fee entry, and the posting date of the latest scheduled-installment payment entry.

**Where are the boundaries?** Hypothetical late fee assessed 2026-06-16: a scheduled-installment payment posted 2026-07-01 is 15 days later and takes 0.8; one posted 2026-06-30 is 14 days later and keeps the share as it is; one posted 2026-07-16 is 30 days later and takes 0.8; one posted 2026-07-17 is 31 days later and takes 0.5.

**A worked figure?** Hypothetical: a late fee of 24.00 with a goodwill share of 0.5 gives 12.00; with 22 days to the payment it is multiplied by 0.8, giving 9.60.
